solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Platform number one in station covered with decaying matter off the wall

indicators.note: the first letter of station is wrapped inside the word for decaying matter, which covers it

parts.note: rot is decaying matter

indicators.note: the number one, or first, letter in the word station

parts.note: off the wall means odd or peculiar, as rum does in British slang

explanation.surface: A rail station's platform one, its wall covered in mould and rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one in' picks S, the first letter of station, and 'covered with' puts it inside ROT. Rum is an old British word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand for a speaker or conductor, a kind of platform.

clue.text: Cancel game, contest between two lightweights?

parts.note: RU is rugby union
a bout is a boxing contest, and lightweight is one boxing weight class

explanation.surface: Calling off a game, a fight between two featherweight figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out is to erase, so to cancel.

clue.text: Suspect at station outwardly arrogant

indicators.note: at here places the outer letters of station in front of the suspect word
outwardly means just the outside letters of station

parts.note: iffy means dubious or suspect

explanation.surface: A suspect at the station looks haughty from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' gives SN, the outer letters of station.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniffy means disdainful or haughty, looking down one's nose.

clue.text: Flatten accumulating earth with stableman's sharp implement

indicators.note: accumulating means the flatten word gathers the others inside it

parts.note: to raze is to flatten a building
the orb is the globe, the earth
a lad is a stable worker who looks after horses

explanation.surface: Flatten the piling soil with the stable-hand's sharp tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accumulating' reads like gathering soil, but it tells the flatten word to take the globe and the stable worker inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin steel blade used in a safety shaver is a sharp tool.

clue.text: PM — accountant leaves island

indicators.note: leaves means the accountant departs from the island

parts.note: Majorca is a Spanish island
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A prime minister, or an accountant fleeing an island.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was British Prime Minister from 1990 to 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: John Major served as Britain's Prime Minister in the 1990s.

clue.text: Strive to get drink back, half emptied by men fighting

indicators.note: back tells us to read the drink word backwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: emptied means the word half loses its inside letters, keeping only its first and last

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a drink back, the glass half emptied by brawling men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SUP into PUS; 'emptied' leaves HF from half. OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword shorthand for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To push for something is to press or strive hard to get it.

clue.text: Improvise drama, extra filling in part

parts.note: a play is a drama
a bye is a cricket extra, a run not scored off the bat

indicators.note: the filling in a word is its central letters, here of part

explanation.surface: Make up a drama, with an extra filling in a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling in' takes AR, the middle of part. A bye is a run in cricket credited when the ball passes the batsman untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: To play by ear is to improvise, acting without a prepared plan.

clue.text: Student beginning to work in boozer

indicators.note: the first letter of work goes in the boozer

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard, a boozer

indicators.note: beginning to work means its first letter

explanation.surface: A student getting down to work in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' suggests the pub, but here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is a student who studies very hard.

clue.text: Source of foul language absorbs American flier

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of foul
absorbs means the language word takes the American abbreviation inside it

parts.note: lingo is slang for a language

explanation.surface: Swearing starts when someone soaks up American slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of foul language' looks like one phrase about swearing; 'Source of' only takes F, and 'absorbs' works on the language word.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a pink wading bird, something that flies.

clue.text: Star may be discovered by this technology item which spices up track

definitions.text: Star may be discovered by this technology

parts.note: rocket is a peppery salad leaf that adds spice
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A tech gadget that adds spice to a running track, and might find a star.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of rockets carries telescopes into space, so it may help find new stars.

clue.text: Offensive second-rate books written by unknown

indicators.note: written by puts the unknown after the other pieces, as in a down light it would sit beneath them

parts.note: B grade is second-rate
lit, short for literature, means books
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: An offensive, second-rate set of books by an anonymous author.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitz is a sudden intense military attack, an offensive.

clue.text: Heroic woman played banjo with head shaven, high-flyers in company recalled

indicators.note: played suggests the remaining letters of the instrument are worked into a new arrangement
the head, or first letter, of banjo is cut off

parts.note: the stringed instrument, as written

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so this piece is read in reverse
the high-flyers sit inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are flyers

explanation.surface: A brave woman played the banjo with a shaved head while airmen in her company were called back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head shaven' leaves ANJO, which 'played' rearranges; 'in' and 'recalled' then make OFARC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maid of Orléans led French forces against the English and is a national heroine.

clue.text: Cheery conman unloading the latest in exercise and six-pack obtainable

parts.note: up means cheerful, as in feeling up

indicators.note: unloading means a letter is dropped from the conman word

parts.note: a forger is a fraudster or conman

indicators.note: the latest, or last, letter in exercise

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles, abs

explanation.surface: A cheerful con artist ditches exercise, and his six-pack is up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the latest in exercise' is E, which 'unloading' removes from FORGER to give FORGR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up for grabs is available for anyone to take, so obtainable.

clue.text: It goes back before the origins of Mother Earth

definitions.text: It goes back before the origins of Mother Earth

indicators.note: goes back means the word it is read in reverse
the origins are the opening letters of the words Mother and Earth

explanation.surface: Something that stretches back to before the planet itself was born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' turns IT into TI; 'the origins of' takes M and E. The whole clue also describes the answer, which predates the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Time existed before the Earth formed, so it reaches back beyond the planet's origins.

clue.text: Brand of car embodies money seen on one island

indicators.note: embodies means the car brand takes the other pieces into its body

parts.note: a marque is a make of car

indicators.note: seen on places the one after the money

parts.note: tin is slang for money
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A car brand's money spotted on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embodies' places the money and the one inside the car brand, splitting it after MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinique is a French Caribbean island.

clue.text: New Orleans contains scope for posh city dweller

indicators.note: contains means the rearranged letters hold the scope word inside them
new means the city name is remade into a fresh order

parts.note: range means scope or extent

explanation.surface: New Orleans has plenty of room for a well-to-do resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the city into SLOANER, and 'contains' puts the scope word before its final R. A Sloane Ranger is an upper-class young Londoner, named after Sloane Square.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a wealthy, conventional young Londoner from Chelsea and Kensington.

clue.text: Furious about European pinching lady's shade

indicators.note: pinching means the furious word grabs the lady inside it
about means the furious word goes around the European letter

parts.note: angry means furious
she is a lady, read as lady is

explanation.surface: An angry European grabs a woman's lampshade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes ANGREY; 'pinching' then holds the lady after its first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen grey is a pale grey colour, a shade.

clue.text: More ridiculous bends on road during Lincoln runs

indicators.note: during means the bends and road sit inside Lincoln's name

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: on places the road after the bends

parts.note: S-bends and U-bends give the letters S and U
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A road with bends during the time Lincoln ran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts SURD inside ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurder means more silly or nonsensical.

clue.text: Single by soprano with excellent set of pipes

indicators.note: by places the soprano next to the single

parts.note: solo means single, alone
top means excellent, the best

explanation.surface: A single by a soprano with a wonderful voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipes' suggests a singing voice, but here they are organ pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo stop on an organ controls a rank of pipes for solo melody.

clue.text: Relations, small in number, describing some horror films

parts.note: blood means family relations, as in blood is thicker than water

indicators.note: the small letter goes inside the number

parts.note: thirty is a number

explanation.surface: Relatives, few in number, feature in certain horror films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside THIRTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gory slasher movies are eager for gore, so they could be called that.

clue.text: Cleaner hoovered perhaps and quit

parts.note: vac is short for vacuum cleaner
to hoover up food is to eat it greedily, so ate

explanation.surface: A cleaner vacuumed and then left the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoovered' looks like cleaning but means ate, as in hoovering up a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate is to leave or quit a place.

clue.text: Out to lunch, French department shares

parts.note: out to lunch is slang for eccentric or odd
Lot is a département in southwest France

explanation.surface: Away at lunch, a French government department divides things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd lot is a block of shares smaller than the standard trading unit.

clue.text: Teacher with uniform that sumo puts away?

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher in uniform, wondering what a sumo wrestler might eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Udon are thick Japanese wheat noodles, the kind of food a sumo wrestler might eat in bulk.

clue.text: Working name represented British joiner, minor trader

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on

indicators.note: represented means the letters of name are presented again in another order

parts.note: and is a joining word, a conjunction

explanation.surface: A working name stood for a British carpenter who runs a small business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges NAME into EMAN. 'joiner' looks like a carpenter but is the linking word AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man band is a small business run by a single person, a small-time trader.

clue.text: Saying 'I'm the greatest' shows priority wrong

indicators.note: the order of precedence is swapped, so the first piece moves to the back

parts.note: taken as written, the letters I and M
max means the most, the greatest

explanation.surface: Boasting you are the greatest only shows your priorities are off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows priority wrong' moves IM from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxim is a short pithy saying or principle.

clue.text: Parking fine daughter settled

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, fine, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: The daughter has paid off her parking fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty but means excellent, A1.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that is paid has been settled.

clue.text: Little female, covering, strains to pick up a particular printer

parts.note: Dot is a girl's name and also means something little
a mat is a floor covering

indicators.note: to pick up means to hear the word, taking it by its sound

parts.note: ricks means strains, as in ricking a neck

explanation.surface: A small woman, wrapped up, struggles to lift a certain printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pick up' signals that RICKS is heard, sounding like RIX.
explanation.definitionFit: This printer forms characters from a grid of tiny pins striking a ribbon, one type of printer.

clue.text: Old writer endlessly probed by a shrink

indicators.note: probed by means the letter A goes into the shortened writer
endlessly means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a quill was an old writing pen

explanation.surface: An old author is endlessly questioned by a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' looks like the psychiatrist but is the verb; 'endlessly' cuts QUILL to QUIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to cower or flinch away in fear.

clue.text: Music sung rhythmically, vainly and quickly

parts.note: rap is music with rhythmic spoken lyrics
idly can mean to no purpose, vainly

explanation.surface: Rhythmic music performed both vainly and fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidly means at speed, fast.

clue.text: Mum, street resident after supplier of milk, potential life-saver

indicators.note: resident after tells us the street sits after the milk supplier

parts.note: ma means mum, mother
a ewe is a female sheep and gives milk

explanation.surface: Mum and a resident of the street waiting for the milkman.
explanation.walkthrough: Wartime airmen called their inflatable life jackets this, after the buxom film star.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was RAF slang for an inflatable life jacket, which could save a life at sea.
